results.result: Processing-resistant Ci variants reveal distinct spatial profiles of Hh-stimulated Ci-155 reduction and inhibition of Ci-155 processing at the AP border.
results.evaluation: Claims C70 and C71 are supported by quantitative analysis of Ci-155 profiles shown in Figure 2. The data demonstrate that Hh-stimulated Ci-155 reduction begins where ptc-lacZ is half-maximal and results in over twofold reduction, while processing inhibition extends in a graded manner across the AP border territory.

results.result: Processing-resistant Ci variants support normal patterns of Hh target gene activation and normal adult wing morphology when supplemented with constitutive Ci repressor, demonstrating that Hh can signal normally without regulated Ci processing.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C4, C5, and C93 are supported by data in Figures 2 and 3 showing that processing-resistant Ci variants (S849A and P(1-3)A) induce normal patterns of ptc-lacZ and En expression at the AP border, and when combined with constitutive Ci repressor (ciCe), produce adults with normally patterned wings. This is a central finding of the manuscript.

results.result: A Ci variant lacking major Rdx/Hib-binding sites (Ci-S3-5) supports normal Hh target gene induction and shows robust Hh-stimulated Ci-155 reduction, suggesting that direct Rdx/Hib binding is not the major mechanism for Ci-155 reduction.
results.evaluation: Claims C72, C73, and C74 are supported by experimental data showing that Ci-S3-5 produces normal wing patterning and maintains robust Ci-155 reduction at the AP border despite lacking major Rdx/Hib binding sites. This challenges the prevailing model that direct Rdx/Hib binding is the primary mechanism for Hh-stimulated Ci-155 degradation.

results.result: Su(fu) is involved in Hh-promoted Ci-155 reduction, as wing discs lacking Su(fu) show no reduction of Ci-155 levels at the AP border.
results.evaluation: Claims C77 and C94 are supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 showing that Ci-155 levels peak at the AP boundary in Su(fu) mutant wing discs, suggesting little or no Hh-stimulated loss. This supports the hypothesis that Su(fu) dissociation from Ci-155 may contribute to pathway-stimulated degradation.

results.result: Artificially activated Fu (GAP-Fu) activates processing-resistant Ci variants more effectively than wild-type Ci, but steady-state Ci-155 levels are similar due to robust degradation, indicating that high pathway activity requires a continuous supply of Ci-155 protected from processing.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C82 are supported by data in Figure 4 showing that GAP-Fu induces higher ptc-lacZ levels with processing-resistant Ci variants than with wild-type Ci, despite similar steady-state Ci-155 levels. This demonstrates that maintaining high pathway activity depends on an adequate supply of unprocessed Ci-155.

results.result: PKA and Cos2 inhibit Ci-155 activity independently of their roles in promoting Ci-155 processing, as demonstrated by increased activity of processing-resistant Ci-P(1-3)A in pka and cos2 mutant clones.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C7, C83, C84, and C9 are supported by data in Figure 5 showing that genetic removal of PKA or Cos2 substantially increases the activity of processing-resistant Ci-P(1-3)A in the absence of Hh. This reveals separate inhibitory roles for these components beyond their established functions in processing.

results.result: The CORD domain of Ci mediates the inhibitory action of Cos2 on Ci-155 activity, as removal of the CORD domain increases activity of processing-resistant Ci and enhances response to PKA loss but not Cos2 loss.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C85, C86, and C87 are supported by data in Figures 6 and 7 showing that deletion of the CORD domain increases Ci-155 activity in pka mutant clones but not in cos2 mutant clones, consistent with the hypothesis that Cos2 inhibits Ci-155 primarily through CORD domain binding.

results.result: The CDN Cos2-binding domain does not alter the activity of processing-resistant Ci, and Ci-155 processing remains efficient without both CDN and CORD domains, confirming that Cos2 binding to the zinc finger domain can suffice for processing.
results.evaluation: Claims C88 and C89 are supported by data in Figures 6 and 7 showing that deletion of the CDN domain does not affect processing-resistant Ci activity, and that Ci lacking both CDN and CORD domains is still efficiently processed. This confirms previous findings about alternative Cos2 binding sites.

results.result: The PKA sites used to direct processing (P1-3) are not essential targets for PKA to inhibit Ci-155 activity, as loss of PKA increases the activity of Ci-P(1-3)A.
results.evaluation: Claim C91 is supported by data in Figure 5 showing that pka mutant clones increase the activity of Ci-P(1-3)A, which lacks the three PKA sites required for processing. This indicates that PKA inhibits Ci-155 through additional phosphorylation sites or mechanisms.

results.result: Removal of the CORD domain reduces En induction at the AP border, potentially due to deficiency in targeting activated Fu to Ci.
results.evaluation: Claim C90 is supported by experimental observation in Figure 7, but the proposed mechanism is speculative. While the data show reduced En induction for Ci-ΔCORD, the hypothesis that this results from deficient Fu targeting requires additional experimental validation.

results.result: Low levels of ptc-lacZ product were detected sporadically in posterior cells when there was a single ci94 allele, representing an experimental artifact.
results.evaluation: Claim C61 is supported by observations in Figure 1 and confirmed by sequencing of the ci94 allele. The authors appropriately identify this as an artifact that does not affect their ability to assay Ci variant activity in anterior cells.

results.result: Background knowledge and prior work on Hedgehog signaling mechanisms, including the roles of Ci/Gli processing, activation, and degradation, as well as the functions of pathway components like Ptc, Smo, Cos2, PKA, Fu, Su(fu), and Rdx/Hib.
results.evaluation: These claims (C1, C2, C10-C58, C62, C63, C66, C67, C75, C76) represent established knowledge from prior literature, appropriately cited throughout the manuscript. They provide necessary context for the current study but are not novel findings from this work.

results.result: Description of Ci variant constructs: Ci-S849A lacks the last CK1 target site and Ci-P(1-3)A has alterations to all three PKA sites.
results.evaluation: Claims C64 and C65 describe the molecular design of Ci variants used in the study. These are methodological details supported by the Materials and methods section and are essential for interpreting the experimental results.

results.result: Summary conclusions: At the AP border, Hh inhibits Ci-155 processing, activates Ci-155, and promotes Ci-155 reduction; Ci-155 not subject to processing is inhibited by PKA and Cos2 (through CORD domain) in addition to Su(fu); and Fu activation requires continued supply of Ci-155 protected from processing.
results.evaluation: Claims C92, C95, and C96 represent summary conclusions synthesizing multiple experimental findings from the study. They are well-supported by the collective data presented in Figures 2-8 and represent the major conceptual advances of the manuscript.
